questions.question: What do checks and balances allow government branches to do?
choices: Limit and influence one another's exercise of power
Exercise every power without outside review
Replace state governments after each election
Choose all voters before an election

questions.question: Which branch can veto legislation passed by Congress?
choices: Judicial branch
State legislative branch
Executive branch
Local judicial branch

questions.question: Which institution can review the constitutionality of government action in a case?
choices: A political party's campaign office
A court with jurisdiction
A private lobbying association
An electoral campaign committee

questions.question: Which chamber confirms many major presidential nominees?
choices: House of Representatives
Both chambers in a joint popular vote
A conference of state governors
Senate

questions.question: Who nominates justices to the U.S. Supreme Court?
choices: President
Chief Justice
Speaker of the House
State governors collectively

questions.question: Which institution controls federal appropriations?
choices: Supreme Court
Electoral College
Congress
Presidential campaign committee

questions.question: Who presides over a Senate impeachment trial of a sitting president?
choices: Vice president
Chief Justice
Secretary of State
Speaker of the House

questions.question: Why does the veto create a legislative-executive check?
choices: The president can permanently prohibit Congress from meeting
Congress must obtain court approval before introducing any bill
A veto makes the president the only national lawmaker
The president can require Congress to reconsider a bill

questions.question: Why can Congress override a veto?
choices: The Constitution preserves a path for strong legislative support to prevail
A veto automatically expires after the next election
The courts must approve every rejected bill
The president has no role in lawmaking

questions.question: How does Senate confirmation check appointment power?
choices: The Senate selects nominees without presidential involvement
Confirmation gives nominees a veto over Congress
Nominees may need support beyond the president alone
Confirmation replaces elections for every federal office

questions.question: How does judicial review check other branches?
choices: Courts can select a new president whenever policy changes
Courts can invalidate actions that violate the Constitution
Judges can pass budgets without Congress
Judges automatically approve executive directives

questions.question: Why is separation of powers not identical to checks and balances?
choices: Both terms describe only state and national power
Checks and balances require one branch to hold all authority
Separation of powers means that branches never interact
Separating responsibilities differs from giving institutions ways to limit each other

questions.question: How can appropriations affect executive policy?
choices: Congress can fund, limit, or decline funding for authorized programs
Congress can pardon federal crimes through a funding vote
Funding votes determine every court verdict
Appropriations eliminate the need for executive administration

questions.question: Why does shared treaty authority illustrate a check?
choices: State governors alone may ratify national treaties
The president may revise any constitutional clause through a treaty
Presidential treaty-making requires the specified Senate consent
The Senate must accept every negotiated treaty

questions.question: Why do checks sometimes slow government action?
choices: The Constitution requires officials never to cooperate
Agreement among institutions may be needed before action proceeds
Every proposal needs a nationwide referendum
All branches must perform exactly the same task

questions.question: The Senate rejects a president's nominee. Which check is operating?
choices: Executive clemency
Judicial precedent
Popular referendum
Advice and consent

questions.question: Congress overrides a veto with the required votes. Which relationship is demonstrated?
choices: A legislative check on executive rejection
An executive check on judicial appointments
A state check on federal criminal trials
A judicial check on treaty negotiations

questions.question: A judge rules that an agency exceeded authority granted by statute. Which check is involved?
choices: Executive review of judicial elections
Legislative ratification of state treaties
Judicial review of executive action
Local approval of federal appropriations

questions.question: Which example shows coordination despite separate powers?
choices: A president ignores every enacted statute
Congress enacts a law that an executive agency implements
A court commands legislators to support one party
The Senate abolishes all presidential elections

questions.question: What question best tests whether a proposed power threatens constitutional checks?
choices: Does the proposal use the most popular campaign slogan?
Does the official personally prefer the policy?
Would the action avoid every public disagreement?
Can another institution lawfully review, limit, or resist its use?
